rationale: Forsa (Aug 4-18, pub Aug 22): Linke 22, CDU 18, AfD 18, Greens 16, SPD 12. Insa (Aug 7-13): CDU 20, Linke 19, AfD 17, Greens 16, SPD 15, and recent polls have rotated CDU/Linke/AfD on top. Wegner resigned and the CDU now runs Stefan Evers; Linke also topped Berlin in the 2025 federal vote.

Real Madrid won 2-1 at Espanyol with a 90th-minute goal on Aug 22 in Mourinho's first game. Atletico beat Malaga 2-0, then drew 2-2 at Villarreal on Aug 23 while fans jeered Alvarez, who wants to leave. The derby is at the Metropolitano and is close to a coin flip.

Yu Yiting set a Chinese record of 2:06.82 at the June nationals, where Yu Zidi was 2nd. She then beat McIntosh to win the Pan Pacs 200 IM in 2:07.45 (Aug 15). Yu Zidi (PB 2:07.41) remains the main threat.

No reports of CPS charges up to Aug 23 (archive and searches). The five long-standing suspects and the unnamed man arrested in Gateshead in 2024 are all still uncharged, so mass is left unassigned for the Gateshead suspect.

Wael Naouar began a 'Sumud hunger strike' in Mornaguia prison on Aug 16, announced Aug 18 (New Arab, ANSA). The support committee said Chennoufi, Henchiri and Boughdiri could join. Their six-month pretrial detention limit falls in mid-September.

Yu Zidi won the 400 IM at the June 19 Chinese nationals in 4:30.79 (8th-fastest performer ever), ahead of Ke Wenxi (4:33.59). Yu Yiting has a 4:33.09 season best, and Narita tied for world silver in 2025 (4:33.26).

Ri Song Gum is the 2023 Asiad champion, set world records in 2025 and is on the DPRK delegation list. Mirabai won CWG 48kg gold and will lift in 49kg at the Asiad (HT, Aug 4). China's entrant is unconfirmed.

Ohashi led most of the Pan Pacs 200 breast final (Aug 15) but faded to bronze in 2:08.27, well off his 2:06.59. China's Asiad roster has Qin Haiyang and Dong Zhihao, and Watanabe is also on Japan's team.

The opener is Portugal v Wales on Sep 24 at Alvalade, reported (Jul 25) as Ronaldo's possible farewell. Ronaldo (scoring for Al Nassr Aug 22) calls 2026-27 'probably my last year' but has not quit Portugal. Draw risk is about 22%.
Still 70 signatories as of Aug 19 (Mauritius was 70th on Jul 17) and no upcoming signers announced. Reaching #75 needs 5 more signings, so the answer stays very diffuse.

Japan's 100m entrants are Shuhei Tada (national champion) and Yuki Koike (10.06, 2026 best); Kiryu is relay-only (JAAF Jun 15). Puripol stays the favourite, and Korea's Nwamadi has run 10.13 (10.07 wind-aided, Aug).

The 6th Cir. panel (Ohio/Tennessee, argued Jul 30) appeared ready to side with the states, and the 4th Cir. Maryland panel (argued May 7) was openly skeptical of Kalshi. The 9th Cir. Nevada appeal is pending, the 2nd Cir. sent Kalshi's CT/NY injunction motions to a panel (Aug 19), and Utah's win (Aug 4) is on appeal to the 10th Cir.

TikTok keeps settling private bellwether cases before trial (three more on Aug 3), but no state settlement yet. Utah's trial is not until June 2027 (Jul 29 order), Pennsylvania sued on Aug 11 and Florida on Jun 15.
Rohit told Vimal Kumar (reported Aug 13) that the 2027 WC is his 'last chance' and he cannot play another. That makes him the likeliest to repeat it inside the Sep 1-20 window.
No new team news. Spain are world champions and England finished 3rd at the WC; Wembley home advantage roughly offsets Spain's rating. The fixture is on Sat Sep 26.

Hamburg withdrew after its referendum failed (54.9% no). The DOSB assembly picks between Berlin, Munich and KoelnRheinRuhr on Sep 26 (MDR, Aug 18). SZ reports federations expect a Munich v Rhine-Ruhr duel, and Rhine-Ruhr's 14M tickets score well in the DOSB matrix. Berlin has no referendum and Wegner has resigned.
AFP (Aug 21) confirms 11-year-old Yuki Kurihara as Japan's Puyo Puyo Champions entrant. He turned pro in April, and Japanese players dominate the game.

Norris won Hungary and then the Dutch GP (Aug 23), so McLaren is back in contention. Antonelli was 2nd and leads Russell and Hamilton by 59 points; Verstappen crashed out. Mercedes' straight-line speed still suits Baku.

Ireland's settlement-goods ban was signed into law on Jul 23, Ireland holds the EU presidency and a services bill follows in September. That makes Ireland the likeliest target for Israeli retaliation. Slovenia was dropped because its new Jansa government plans to reverse recognition (Jun 28).

Sindhu lost a close Worlds R16 to Wang Zhiyi (Aug) after winning the Japan Open in July. Badminton runs Sep 20-29, so the Sep 27 resolution date lines up with quarterfinal day (resolved questions have resolution dates equal to the exit date).

NST (Aug 6): Sivasangari is world No. 5 and won the Australian Open and Grasshopper Cup this year, while Watanabe is No. 6 and plays at home. Anahat Singh (No. 20) won the World Junior title on Jul 25. Malaysia's second singles entrant is Aifa Azman.

Defending champion Ng Eain Yow (No. 18) has struggled on the PSA tour this year (NST Aug 6). His named rivals are Abhay Singh (No. 24), Noor Zaman (No. 29), Veer Chotrani (No. 38), Velavan Senthilkumar and Al-Tamimi.

The Sep 27 match in Debrecen is open to spectators with a small Israeli allocation, and the FAI will not seek tickets for Irish fans (Aug 4/14). Ireland remain slight favourites with little venue edge for either side.

Florida sued OpenAI on Jun 1; OpenAI removed it to federal court (Judge Cannon) and Florida is seeking remand. On Aug 4 a 15-state Republican AG coalition (incl. FL, TX, UT, MO) demanded OpenAI stop the testing behind the rogue-agent breach. NY and CO lead a separate multistate probe.
No new information, so the forecast is unchanged. France (Zidane) play away at Turkiye (Sep 25) and Belgium (Sep 28, new coach Van Bommel), and Turkiye host both their games.

Pathirage beat Neeraj at Lausanne on Aug 21 (88.14 v 88.05), his third win over him in 2026 after Rome and CWG gold. Arshad finished outside the top 3 there. Rohit Yadav (87.05 SB) is on India's team.

Krack (Aug 20) says Aston Martin is 'fairly confident' of renewing Alonso, and The Race (Aug 21) says the direction of travel points to an extension. Alonso is still deciding and may take another role. Sainz (Williams, Aug 19) and Verstappen (Red Bull to 2030) are off the market.

Medias24 (Jul 23) says Istiqlal is no longer the clear favourite: PAM has momentum after recruiting Lekjaa, and RNI (led by Chaouki since Feb 7, Akhannouch still central) has the strongest machine. ExpressTV (Aug 11) frames it as an RNI v PAM duel; the vote is Sep 23.

China (2026 U23 Asian Cup runners-up) drew Group B with North Korea (Sep 16), Iran (Sep 20) and UAE (Sep 23). The QF is Sep 26 and the SF Sep 30 in Osaka, so the Sep 30 resolution date points to a semi-final exit. Mass goes to likely SF opponents: Japan on one bracket, Korea/Uzbekistan/Saudi/Vietnam on the other.
